text:
maya: Heads-up — I'm flying into town for the conference next week. Any quick tips for surviving a soggy week? umbrella vs lightweight rain jacket vs poncho? laundromat recs? trying to avoid soggy shoes :sweat_smile:

jamie: Jacket + packable hood every time. Umbrella is ok but juggling badge + bag + drink is a nightmare. Poncho only if you know you'll be outside for hours.

omar: Foldable umbrella + merino socks. If your shoes get soaked, stuff with paper towels, let them dry with a hairdryer on low in the morning. There's a laundromat on 3rd & Elm (Wash&Go) that's cheap and open late.

sree: Pro tip: keep a small ziplock of baking soda for on-the-go shoe stink fixes. Quick-dry towel is clutch. Also I wear an extra pair of cheap sneakers for the plane in case I need to swap.

ben: Dryer sheets in the luggage keep shirts fresh. Also bring a few large zip bags for wet clothes.

maya: Any thoughts on bike/scooter commuting in rain for offsite dinners? want to avoid arriving soaked.

jamie: Bikes are fine with pannier + rain cover, scooters = no (slippery). Rideshare if you want to be dry and fast.

omar: Venue had free coat racks last year but lines got long around 6:30pm. Hotel concierge storage is a bigger time-saver if you're nearby.

sree: Also check the door entry: some hotels have a full-length umbrella rack you can borrow. :thumbsup:

maya: Solid — quick poll (emoji): react with :umbrella: if you prefer umbrella, :coat: if you prefer jacket, or just reply.

ben: I'm leaving Thursday morning fwiw.

travel-bot: Reminder: check-in opens 24h before your flight. Set an alarm!
